plan.title: Within-subject DE: control vs treated_A vs treated_B
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a repeated-measures design: 4 subjects each contribute a control, a treated_a, and a treated_b sample (single batch, 12 samples total, 12000 genes, raw Salmon counts). The correct model is a paired/blocked analysis that accounts for subject as a covariate — a standard two-group unpaired test would waste power and risk confounding by inter-subject variability. Track 1 builds one DESeq2 model with ~subject + condition to answer three linked questions: (1) which genes change under treated_a vs control, (2) which genes change under treated_b vs control (either treatment vs control, pooled via a likelihood-ratio test against the null of no condition effect, giving a defensible 'responds to either treatment' gene set), and (3) which genes differ between treated_a and treated_b directly. Track 2 takes the significant gene sets forward into WikiPathways human pathway enrichment to interpret what each contrast and the A-vs-B contrast mean biologically. Track 3 is a lightweight sanity/QC step (PCA, dispersion, sample correlation) run first so the paired model's assumptions (consistent within-subject pairing, no obvious outlier sample) are checked before drawing conclusions from only 4 subjects — a small n where a single mislabeled or outlier sample would dominate results.
